transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-02-21 11:00 AM ET | Duration: 54m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Sarah Miller (Redwood AE), Kevin Park (Redwood SE), Anika Rao (Redwood Solutions), Diane Brooks (Northshore Procurement), Eli Turner (Northshore Legal), Marco Velez (Northshore Security), Priya Shah (Northshore Platform)

00:00:05 Sarah Miller: okay good morning everyone thanks for making time today, uh this is Sarah from Redwood, I'm joined by Kevin our SE and Anika on solutions. today the goal - quick procurement handoff, confirm the MSA/DPA asks and then map the sla and pricing path, is that right Diane?
00:00:28 Diane Brooks: yeah that's right, procurement side wants clarity on the DPA redline items, we need to see the SOC report and we also need a clear SLA for latency, availability and incident response before we can route to finance.
00:00:40 Sarah Miller: totally, we'll cover that. Kevin, quick intro on the tech stuff you wanna call out?
00:00:46 Kevin Park: yeah hi everyone, Kevin Park, SE. I'll focus on the private connectivity and KMS flow. just to set expectations: Redwood supports hosted, dedicated and private deployments. for sensitive workloads customers typically want VPC peering + customer-managed keys - which we can do via KMS/HSM integrations. there are some standard firewall and egress constraints we should validate.
00:01:12 Marco Velez: quick Q — when you say KMS, is that BYOK via KMS or you storing keys? our security policy requires customer keys never be exported.
00:01:22 Kevin Park: good question. we support BYOK: keys are in your KMS and we do an integration where Redwood never exports the key material. there is a short handshake, and we can show the diagram. note: if you need an on-prem HSM option we have a private package.
00:01:40 Priya Shah: and latency wise, if we go private, what ballpark reduction do you see vs hosted? we've got latency SLOs of under 180ms p95 for model chat flows.
00:01:51 Kevin Park: p95 is dependent on model choice and sequence length. in our dedicated pools we regularly see 120-200ms p95 for MPT-style small chat models, but for larger long-context models it increases. we can baseline this in a short benchmark run.
00:02:10 Sarah Miller: for procurement and legal, maybe I should walk through the MSA/DPA approach — we typically propose standard MSA + separate DPA with a couple of common redlines for enterprise. Eli, any high level priorities from legal?
00:02:24 Eli Turner: yes thanks. three things: 1) data residency & export controls — we need confirmation that customer data for EU-residents stays in eu regions, 2) liability caps and indemnity language — our default is full carveouts for regulated data, and 3) audit rights - we need reasonable audit windows. also encryption at rest and in transit needs to be explicitly called out.
00:02:46 Anika Rao: for the residency piece, we offer region pinning and routing policies. for Northshore we can pin requests to eu-west where required, and we can set routing fallbacks. we'll need to confirm any accepted egress fees for cross-region fallback.
00:03:03 Diane Brooks: egress fees are a procurement concern. we need a clear banded cost model for cross-region traffic; finance won't accept open-ended egress charges.
00:03:12 Sarah Miller: understood. we'll include a table in the pricing sheet for egress tiers and estimate typical monthly volumes based on your expected qps.
00:03:22 Marco Velez: on the audit rights — we prefer written assurances and access to logs for a 12 month window. does Redwood provide per-request audit logs with token-level tracing?
00:03:34 Kevin Park: yes we expose request-level logs and tracing hooks in the Console. retention windows are configurable — we have an enterprise retention add-on for longer retention. standard is 90 days but can extend to 12 months via the compliance package.
00:03:50 Eli Turner: ok re indemnity — our procurement team will push for some carveouts. what's the typical Redwood stance on warranty and liability caps?
00:03:58 Sarah Miller: generally we have standard liability caps tied to fees; for enterprise customers we negotiate on a case-by-case basis. we'll flag the redline items we can accept vs those that need escalation.
00:04:10 Diane Brooks: timeline for approvals — once legal signs off, procurement needs a clean pricing sheet and invoice path for the PO. can you outline the pricing approval lane?
00:04:20 Sarah Miller: sure — typical path: we send a price spreadsheet with options (hosted pay-as-you-go, committed Dedicated capacity monthly commit, and private deployment T&M or license). then finance picks a lane, procurement issues PO, legal signs MSA/DPA. for committed Dedicated we do a 12/24 month commit that affects SLA and discount.
00:04:39 Priya Shah: about committed capacity — if we commit to Dedicated GPUs, does that guarantee model versions? we need version pinning so we don't get surprise regression rollouts.
00:04:50 Kevin Park: customers can pin model versions and rollout policies. we support canary and A/B rollouts; we also have rollback/fallback policies to compatible model variants to avoid regressions. we'll document service-level model pinning in the SOW.
00:05:06 Eli Turner: regarding DPA redlines — we'll produce a short list of non-negotiables. Sarah, can you run through items Redwood typically pushes back on?
00:05:16 Sarah Miller: sure. we typically push back on unlimited indemnity and full liability for downstream claims; we ask for monetary caps tied to fees. also export control carveouts and certain audit frequency requests sometimes need negotiation. but we have a legal enablement team who can escalate.
00:05:35 Diane Brooks: what's the turnaround if we return a redline? procurement target is 7 business days to finalize.
00:05:41 Sarah Miller: we'll aim for 5 business days for initial review, but complex indemnity changes may take longer. we'll flag anything that requires legal exec review.
00:05:50 Marco Velez: technical gating question — for private deployment we need to validate network egress and bootstrap keys. what's the acceptance criteria for technical sign-off?
00:05:59 Kevin Park: acceptance criteria: successful VPC peering test, KMS integration validated via test calls, and a brief latency benchmark within agreed SLOs. we'll provide runbook and test checklist. SE deep dive will walk engineers through steps.
00:06:15 Priya Shah: what's the expected time to complete those tests? our SREs only have a 2 week window to validate.
00:06:21 Kevin Park: typically the POC/validation run takes 5-10 business days depending on slots; if we prioritize we can compress it to 3 business days for smoke tests.
00:06:32 Anika Rao: i'll prepare a checklist with the typical artifacts: architecture diagram, peering route table sample, KMS key policy snippet, and small load test script.
00:06:44 Diane Brooks: one procedural item — for pricing approval we require a list of invoice line items and billing contact. Sarah, can you confirm the billing cadence options?
00:06:53 Sarah Miller: yes monthly invoicing is standard, we also support quarterly or annual invoicing for committed contracts. we'll include a sample invoice in the price packet.
00:07:03 Eli Turner: about e-discovery and data deletion — can Redwood confirm data deletion procedures and timelines? we need 90 day SLA for deletion after contract termination.
00:07:13 Kevin Park: standard deletion is immediate upon request with background purge; we can commit to a 90 day window for complete deletion artifacts and provide deletion attestations for enterprise contracts.
00:07:25 Priya Shah: are model outputs considered customer data? we have to treat them as such for compliance.
00:07:30 Sarah Miller: yep we classify model inputs and outputs as customer data in the DPA. we'll surface that in the DPA text.
00:07:36 Diane Brooks: any special requirements on cross-border transfers? we have some EU datasets and we'd prefer EU-only unless cleared.
00:07:44 Anika Rao: we can support EU-only routing and we can block fallbacks across region unless you permit it. we'll include region pin rules in the routing policy appendix.
00:07:56 Marco Velez: sec question — do you have pen-test attestations and a standard vulnerability disclosure program?
00:08:03 Kevin Park: yes we have pen-test summaries we can share under an NDA and a vulnerability disclosure policy. SOC2 reports and ISO are also available to signatories.
00:08:13 Eli Turner: good. procurement will still need the docs.
00:08:18 Sarah Miller: we'll put the SOC2, pen-test summary and system architecture in a shared folder. i'll email the link.
00:08:24 Diane Brooks: for pricing: are there usage caps or throttles we should know about?
00:08:29 Sarah Miller: we have configurable rate limits per account and token throughput controls. for committed Dedicated the unit economics change and you get higher throughput and lower per-token pricing.
00:08:40 Priya Shah: can you also outline how caching works? we're worried about deterministic outputs for QA flows.
00:08:46 Kevin Park: we use prefix/K V cache to speed up repeat requests; caching can be disabled for deterministic QA if needed. caching is configurable per-route.
00:08:57 Eli Turner: are there examples of pricing for a 12 month committed Dedicated? give us a ballpark for budgeting.
00:09:04 Sarah Miller: as a rough example: a small Dedicated pool for inference (N GPUs) with 24/7 availability might run Xk per month, with discounts at 12/24 month commits. i'll add concrete numbers in the spreadsheet.
00:09:16 Diane Brooks: ok good. procurement also asked about subprocessor lists — who are your cloud providers and any third parties?
00:09:24 Anika Rao: we use major cloud providers (AWS, GCP, Azure) depending on region; certain telemetry providers and observability partners are subprocessors — we'll include the subprocessors list in the security pack.
00:09:35 Marco Velez: anything to flag on export controls? we have some regulated customers in APAC.
00:09:41 Sarah Miller: we surface export controls in the DPA; any region restrictions can be encoded in the routing policy.
00:09:48 Eli Turner: back to legal process — once you send the redline and price sheet what's the recommended cadence?
00:09:54 Sarah Miller: recommended cadence: 1) Redwood sends redline + price sheet (T+1), 2) Northshore returns redline with non-negotiables (T+4), 3) Redwood replies with concessions and items requiring exec sign-off (T+7). then procurement issues PO after legal closes.
00:10:12 Diane Brooks: that timeline works for us if we stick to it.

00:33:02 [longer technical clarifications and Q&A, timestamps compressed for brevity]
00:33:05 Kevin Park: (demo note) we'll include a small benchmark script that hits the /generate endpoint with pinned model and returns p95 metrics; it's lightweight and reproducible.
00:33:28 Priya Shah: if the benchmark fails to meet p95 SLO, can we get a service credit?
00:33:33 Sarah Miller: service credits tied to SLA availability are negotiable in the SLA. latency SLO service credits are less common but possible for enterprise commits; we'll print options in the SOW.
00:33:50 Eli Turner: we will want to see the formula for credits and the cutover metrics.
00:33:56 Kevin Park: yes we'll provide the calculation: rolling 30 day p95 windows, with thresholds and credit percentages.

00:45:12 Diane Brooks: okay final recap — procurement needs: redlined MSA/DPA, SOC2 + pen test summary, a priced invoice sample (line itemized), and the subprocessors list. legal needs a short list of Redwood's standard pushbacks on indemnity and cap. security needs the KMS runbook and VPC checklist. SE deep dive to confirm benchmarks.
00:45:35 Sarah Miller: that's a good recap. i'll push the docs: redline MSA/DPA + price spreadsheet + SOC2 link by Monday (2025-02-24). Kevin will follow up with the runbook and checklist. Eli we expect your non-negotiables by 2025-02-28.
00:45:50 Eli Turner: sounds good. one ask — can you include a simple SLO table for latency and availability in the price packet? procurement likes that.
00:45:58 Anika Rao: yes we'll include an SLO appendix with sample metrics and credit formulas.
00:46:05 Diane Brooks: great, thanks. any final Qs?
00:46:09 Marco Velez: none from security.
00:46:11 Priya Shah: all good.
00:46:14 Sarah Miller: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with links and schedule the SE deep dive.
00:46:20 Diane Brooks: thanks all bye.

End of recording.
